paper.title_en: Phase-space structure and chaos of a confined massless particle around rotating Bumblebee Kerr–Newman–AdS black holes
paper.abstract_en: Spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking by a bumblebee vector field modifies the geometry of rotating, charged black holes. We study how this modification, together with a negative cosmological constant <math altimg="si367.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3787"><mi>Λ</mi></math>, affects a massless test particle with zero azimuthal angular momentum confined by an external harmonic potential around a rotating bumblebee Kerr–Newman–AdS black hole. Without the potential the null geodesic flow admits a Carter-type constant and is integrable for every value of the bumblebee parameter <math altimg="si432.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3792"><mi>α</mi></math> and of <math altimg="si367.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3797"><mi>Λ</mi></math>, so it is the confinement, not Lorentz violation, that breaks integrability; we identify the integrable limits of the confined system and derive the normal variational equation along its invariant axial solution. At fixed energy, Poincaré sections on two transverse surfaces with 2000 crossings per orbit, rotation-number profiles, Lyapunov exponents from the variational equations up to <math altimg="si346.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3803"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and the smaller alignment index reveal a mixed phase space of KAM tori, island chains at the resonances <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3824"><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> and thin chaotic layers, already present at <math altimg="si376.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3846"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. For <math altimg="si7.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3856"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≤</mo><mi>α</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≤</mo><mn>0.07</mn></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si8.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3871"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.005</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≤</mo><mi>Λ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> the chaotic fraction of the surface of section, compared after the same number of radial periods, is about 16% and consistent with a constant (fitted changes of <math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3887"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></math> percentage points across each range), with the same behaviour at the other energies studied; Kerr–Newman–AdS black holes with the rescaled parameters <math altimg="si265.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3899"><mrow><mi>Λ</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si266.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3918"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> give consistent fractions. The finite-time Lyapunov exponents of chaotic orbits are about 1% of the horizon surface gravity, far below the chaos bound. What <math altimg="si432.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3938"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math altimg="si367.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3943"><mi>Λ</mi></math> change is the position of the resonances: by increasing <math altimg="si14.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3948"><msub><mrow><mi>Δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> in the region of the trap they raise the radial frequency more than the polar one, lower the rotation number and move the island chains towards the axial orbit. For <math altimg="si432.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3958"><mi>α</mi></math>, the comparison with the rescaled Kerr–Newman–AdS black holes shows that this shift is produced by the solid-angle-deficit term specific to the bumblebee background. Recurrence quantification of orbit ensembles is consistent with this picture. Within this model, Lorentz violation reorganises the resonant structure of phase space, but it is not the source of chaos and does not change its extent by more than about two percentage points. •We study test-particle dynamics in the spacetime of a rotating Bumblebee Kerr–Newman–Anti-de Sitter black hole, where Lorentz symmetry breaking is controlled by the bumblebee parameter.•Orbital dynamics is analysed via Poincaré sections, maximum Lyapunov exponents, and recurrence analysis.•The phase space shows transitions between regular and chaotic behaviour depending on system parameters and initial conditions.•Positive saturated Lyapunov exponents reveal exponential separation of nearby trajectories.•The recurrence plots display fragmented diagonals and complex recurrence domains indicative of chaos.
